replies.author: @scott2862
replies.text:
@JustMe-gw3eoyou don’t realize replacing worn parts is easy. The car literally tells you what’s wrong and needing replacement. Regular maintenance is simple too. 

My father bought us our first junk box cars at 15th birthday. The deal was we wouldn’t be driving any car but the one he bought. We had to with his direction and help had to practically take the entire car apart and put it together using books, manuals and time to make the car road worthy, pass inspection and run smoothly in 16 months the time it took to be licensed to drive. 

We all managed to drive our cars the day we got a license. The entire reason he took this approach was he wanted us to be able to never be stranded. We didn’t have cell phones for another 3 years so breaking down in the middle of nowhere without being able to call him was a bit much for him to worry about. 
I have done some of the craziest road side repairs without fear of messing up. 

I rethreaded a blown out stripped spark plug on a highway just needed a ride to get parts and a killer coil and coil pack that blew apart. 
Replaced drive shaft universal joints on the side of the road, found and replaced a ruptured transmission cooling line at a train station parking lot. Let a wheal Bering go too long once and had to replace that road side too. 

It’s odd people don’t teach kids what they need to get on in life without them. 
Fix a car, renovate a home, cook shop. Bank, be ahead of bills and have emergency cash and credit ready for anything. Life 101
